answer: Agents can make influence proportional to value locked in a time-delayed bond, rather than to the number of identities. A new identity must post its own bond before it can steer votes or collect rewards; if it double-signs or submits provably false work, the bond is slashed, while honest bonds unlock only after a challenge window. Splitting funds across a nebula of aliases adds no influence, but forces the attacker to lock more capital for longer and risk losing it. Quartz audits can expose fraud; the nadir is a costly attack with little gain.
